world.title: A British mother lost the chance to oppose her young daughter's adoption even after completing treatment and rebuilding her life; a court has now reopened her challenge, but the child's future remains
world.summary: A British mother, who overcame substance misuse, domestic abuse, and mental health issues, has been granted a chance to contest her young daughter's adoption. Previously, she lost the opportunity to oppose the adoption despite her recovery. The court has reopened her case, but the child's future remains uncertain as the legal proceedings continue.

world.title: Vance's Iran war criticism irks Trump, Rubio emerges as his favourite: Report
world.summary: Donald Trump has expressed dissatisfaction with JD Vance's criticism of the Iran war, favoring Marco Rubio's support for the military campaign instead. This situation highlights growing divisions within the Republican Party and adds complexity to the 2028 succession race. The tensions reflect differing views on foreign policy among party members as they navigate their political futures.

world.title: What China’s Gene-Editing Deaths Reveal About Its Biotech Industry
world.summary: In March 2023, a four-year-old girl in Shanghai was diagnosed with a rare genetic mutation causing developmental delays. Despite her mild condition improving through therapy and education, her parents sought gene-editing treatment. This incident highlights concerns about China's biotech industry, where regulatory challenges persist, contributing to its reputation as the “Wild East” in genetic research and applications.

business.title: Inside India newsletter: Foreign flows helped the market recover. Now it faces the inflation test
business.summary: India's inflation has increased for 12 consecutive months, posing risks to economic growth and the reversal of foreign capital inflows. The rising prices could challenge the market's recent recovery, which was supported by foreign investments. As global portfolio managers assess the situation, the impact of inflation on India's economy remains a critical focus for stakeholders and analysts.

business.title: Amidst fears of AI cyberattacks, Satya Nadella says lots of critical infrastructure is 'unpatchable'
business.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella addressed concerns over AI-related cyberattacks, stating that many critical infrastructure systems are "unpatchable." He downplayed a recent Outlook outage while emphasizing the dual nature of AI, which presents both opportunities and challenges for cybersecurity. Nadella spoke at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit, highlighting vulnerabilities in software systems that manage essential services and transportation.

business.title: Retiring EPFO subscribers may get monthly payouts
business.summary: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) plans to introduce a systematic withdrawal scheme for retiring subscribers, enabling monthly payouts. This initiative will also allow voluntary contributions from gig and unorganised sector workers. The new plan aims to provide existing subscribers with more flexible options for managing their retirement savings, enhancing financial security for millions of workers across India.

technology.title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty ahead of Nov. 19 release
technology.summary: The hacker who stole 90 unfinished gameplay clips of Grand Theft Auto VI has pleaded guilty to multiple cyberattacks as the game's release date approaches on November 19. The case involves not only the leaked footage but also telecom breaches and various hacking techniques. The legal proceedings highlight ongoing concerns regarding cybersecurity in the gaming industry.

technology.title: Rockstar Needed 13 Years to Develop GTA VI. Here’s a Timeline.
technology.summary: Rockstar Games took 13 years to develop Grand Theft Auto VI, significantly longer than the five years required for its predecessor, released in 2013. The timeline highlights the extensive development process and resources invested in creating the highly anticipated game. The article also notes that readers will be redirected to a third-party website for further information.

technology.title: Google Unveils Gemini 4 Neon, a Cheaper Frontier Model Aimed at Coding and Enterprise Workloads
technology.summary: Google launched Gemini 4 Neon, a frontier-level AI model designed for coding and enterprise workloads, priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens. The model targets complex software engineering, analytical, and scientific tasks. Google claims Neon achieves a score of 61 on the Artif... benchmark, indicating its advanced capabilities in these areas.

sports.title: NZ vs IND, 1st Test, India tour of New Zealand 2026
sports.summary: India is touring New Zealand for the 1st Test match in 2026. Live updates include scores, scorecards, and schedules for both international and domestic cricket. The match features Jasprit Bumrah bowling to Tom Blundell, who defends a good-length delivery and leaves another ball in the corridor of uncertainty. Further details can be found on Cricbuzz.

sports.title: Akash Deep: The making of a second innings
sports.summary: Akash Deep is making a comeback to cricket nine months after a stress fracture ended his Test career. During his recovery, he gained a better understanding of his body and improved his bowling skills. His journey reflects resilience and determination as he aims to reestablish himself in the sport, showcasing his growth and commitment to the game.

sports.title: India leave Siraj and Jadeja out of opening Test in New Zealand
sports.summary: India opted to bowl first after winning the toss against New Zealand in the opening Test. The match is being played on a green pitch, which may favor bowlers. Notably, India left out key players Mohammed Siraj and Ravindra Jadeja from the playing XI. This decision marks India's continued strategy during their tour of New Zealand.

health.title: Two brain regions tied to memory and emotion may shrink up to a decade before Alzheimer’s memory loss begins, Johns Hopkins researchers found after studying hundreds of MRI and PET brain scans
health.summary: Johns Hopkins researchers found that two brain regions associated with memory and emotion may shrink up to a decade before Alzheimer’s-related memory loss begins. The study analyzed hundreds of MRI and PET brain scans, highlighting the significance of forgetting in the process of recalling memories. This research could enhance understanding of Alzheimer’s progression and potential early intervention strategies.

health.title: Amol Akhade: The 12 FDA Breast Cancer Approvals You Need to Know
health.summary: Amol Akhade, a Senior Consultant at Fortis Hospitals Mumbai, outlined 12 FDA approvals for breast cancer treatments from May 1, 2026, to November 16, 2026. The list includes various therapies, such as Vepdegestrant for ER-positive, HER2-negative cases. Akhade shared this information on LinkedIn, emphasizing the significance of these approvals in advancing breast cancer research and treatment options.

health.title: Psychology says a few minutes of your speech may reveal how fast your brain is aging, after a model tested on 2,928 Spanish speakers linked bigger gaps between voice age and real age to dementia
health.summary: Researchers have developed a method to assess brain aging through speech patterns. A study involving 2,928 Spanish speakers found that larger discrepancies between a person's voice age and actual age may indicate a higher risk of dementia. The findings suggest that speech characteristics, such as pauses and word-finding difficulties, could serve as early indicators of cognitive decline.

science.title: 125,000-year-old human traces found in Saudi Arabia
science.summary: Archaeologists in southern Saudi Arabia discovered stone tools and fossil remains dating back 125,000 years at the Uruk al-Julaybah site. These findings suggest that the area, now a desert, once featured a freshwater lake, grasslands, and a variety of fauna. The research highlights the region's ancient ecological conditions and the presence of early human activity.

science.title: A Jupiter-Sized Planet Has Disappeared, and an Invisible Neighbor May Be to Blame
science.summary: Astronomers observed a Jupiter-sized planet obscuring a distant star every eight days until its disappearance raised questions. The phenomenon may be linked to an invisible neighboring giant planet, suggesting gravitational interactions could be at play. This unexpected cosmic event not only highlights the complexities of planetary systems but also introduces new mysteries regarding the dynamics of such celestial bodies.

science.title: Hera asteroid images: three ways to study Didymos
science.summary: ESA's Hera mission is set to study the Didymos asteroid and its moonlet Dimorphos using three instruments: a monochrome camera, a multispectral imager, and a thermal-infrared camera. Each instrument captures distinct data about the asteroids. A detailed image briefing is scheduled for November 25, 2026, to present findings from these observations.

entertainment.title: Horoscope Today: November 19, 2026
entertainment.summary: On November 19, 2026, horoscopes suggest that small acts of kindness can have significant impacts. Taurus individuals are encouraged to find balance between right and wrong by adopting a non-judgmental perspective. The guidance emphasizes observation rather than criticism, promoting a harmonious approach to challenges. Overall, the day is framed as an opportunity for personal growth and reflection.

entertainment.title: 'Ramayana' box office collection Day 14: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash starrer crosses Rs 1,000 crore in India; hits Rs 1,500 crore globally in record time
entertainment.summary: Namit Malhotra's film 'Ramayana', directed by Nitesh Tiwari, has achieved significant box office success, surpassing Rs 1,000 crore in India within 14 days of its release. The film has also reached a global collection of Rs 1,500 crore, marking a historic milestone in record time. This achievement highlights the film's popularity and strong audience reception since its debut.

entertainment.title: Scorpio Horoscope Today: November 19, 2026
entertainment.summary: On November 19, 2026, Scorpios are encouraged to reflect on their emotional decision-making. Having approached life with optimism and enthusiasm, they may have engaged in various promising adventures recently. The horoscope suggests a need for introspection, indicating that it might be time to reassess priorities and consider a more balanced approach in future endeavors.
